priority.summary: Fermi Inc. has issued $431.25 million in aggregate principal amount of 5.00% convertible senior notes due 2031, with total net proceeds of approximately $416.81 million, which will be used for general corporate purposes. The notes are convertible into cash, shares of common stock, or a combination thereof, and have a conversion rate initially set at 105.0862 shares of common stock per $1,000 principal amount of notes. The company also entered into capped call transactions to reduce potential dilution to its common stock upon conversion of the notes, using approximately $34.5 million of the net proceeds to pay for these transactions.

priority.summary: Fermi Inc. discloses the immediate resignation of director Miles Everson, effective July 10, 2026, due to a disagreement over access to company books and records and the delegation of responsibility for overseeing financing transactions to the Finance Committee. Everson, a designee of Toby Neugebauer, did not serve on any committee of the Board at the time of his resignation. The company believes Everson was granted full access to its books and records, except for materials related to pending litigation involving Neugebauer.

Neugebauer, co-founder and largest shareholder of Fermi Inc., disclosed that the company has dropped its lawsuit against him, which was filed in response to his challenge of the validity of the company's 70% supermajority bylaw. This move comes after the Texas Business Court ordered Fermi to produce documents and testimony explaining the rationale for the bylaw, and Neugebauer claims that the company's decision to abandon the lawsuit confirms that the bylaw was adopted to entrench the board's power. Neugebauer's claims challenging the validity of the bylaw remain alive and he will continue to pursue discovery and depositions of key players.
